paras.text: Definition: Future Perfect Continuous tense, also known as Future Perfect Progressive tense is used to talk about an action that will have begun in past , present or future and that will continue up for some indefinite time in future.
paras.urdu: تعریف: مستقبل مکمل جاری، جسے مستقبل مکمل استمراری بھی کہا جاتا ہے، ایسے کام کے بارے میں بات کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو ماضی، حال یا مستقبل میں شروع ہو چکا ہو گا اور مستقبل میں کسی غیر معین وقت تک جاری رہے گا۔
paras.pashto: تعریف: راتلونکی بشپړ روان زمان، چې د راتلونکي بشپړ دوامداره زمان په نوم هم پېژندل کېږي، د داسې کار په اړه د خبرو لپاره کارول کېږي چې په تېر، اوسني یا راتلونکي وخت کې به پیل شوی وي او په راتلونکي کې به تر یو نامعلوم وخته دوام ومومي.

sections.theory:
I will have had my lunch by 1 p.m.

I will have finished when you arrive.

It is important to remember that in future perfect tense, the action you are talking about, must have a deadline. If you don't mention a deadline then it is better to use the simple future tense instead of the future perfect tense.

For example,

"Hoorain will leave."(correct) instead of "Hoorain will have left".(incorrect), but

Hoorainwillhaveleftbeforeevening.(Correct)

Activity

Divide the class into several groups of five students each. Ask them to write five sentences on the topic "what will our country be like in the next 50 years ? What will have happened by then?" They should be advised to use the future perfect in their sentences.

For example,' people will have got more artificial by then.'

Activity

Use the correct form of the verbs in the brackets to make it future perfect tense:

1. Umair____his bike next week. (To repair)

2. They____the washing by by 9 o'clock. ( To do)

3. He____Malaysia by the end of this year. ( To visit )

4. I____by 9 o'clock.( To finish)

5. The police_ the thief. (To arrest)

6. She____in the concert tomorrow evening.( To play)

7. By this time nextyear, Abrar_his University degree. (To take)

9. When I get home my dog____at the door watching for me. ( To sit)

10. The train____before we reach the station. (To leave)

11. She____this issue with her father tonight. ( To discuss)

sections.theory:
Actually, in Future Perfect Continuous tense, we go in our imagination to a future point and from there, we talk about an ongoing action that for how long it has been continuing with reference to a particular point of time/activity and that particular point/activity might be now or even before now.

Consider the following timeline:

Suppose you are now in 2020; and let's say you started teaching English right this year; you are thinking about the next year 2021(future) ; so you would say, " Next year I will have been teaching English for one year." But if suppose you started the job back in 2016 then thinking about the next year (2021) you would say,

" Next year I will have been teaching English for five years."

Here, " will have been teaching" indicates that the action of teaching will be continuing up to the next year (2021) and might go even further.

Unlike Future Perfect tense, the action here has no end date or completion point.

Identity:

To Identify the Future Perfect Continuous tense, it is to remember that this tense has the following form or structure.

Subject + will + have+ been+ present participle of the main verb

Fe example,

He will have been playing hockey for three years by the next week.

They will have been sleeping for two hours when their father gets home.

Shama will have been doing her job for two years the next month.

They will have been playing football for hours before you reach.

I will have been helping him for a few hours at night.

Learning activity:

Ask your students to imagine themselves 20 years in future from now (2040). Have each one write 5 sentences about what he or she will have been doing at that time; and for how long between now and then.

For example, " I will have been working on a good position for 15 years."
